name: Bunker Obsidis
specific_features: Extensive underground bunker complex of recent construction
Concealed ship berths within hollow magma chambers
description: Bunker Obsidis is a small, dark world whose surface is almost entirely coated in ancient obsidian lava flows, giving it an albedo so low that it is difficult to detect against the background void. Impact craters have been glazed over with impact glass, creating shallow bowls that gleam faintly under starlight. Beneath the surface, hollow magma chambers from the planet's volcanic past provide vast, naturally enclosed spaces.

The absence of atmosphere makes Bunker Obsidis a world of stark visual contrasts -- the obsidian surface absorbs light almost completely, while impact glass craters reflect it in concentrated points. From orbit, the planet resembles a dark sphere peppered with stars of its own. The surface is eerily smooth in the lava flow regions, the obsidian having cooled into vast, glassy sheets that ring under footfall.

Someone has been building here. Deep-penetrating scans revealed an extensive underground complex within the magma chambers, constructed with materials and methods suggesting a well-funded operation within the last century. Ship berths capable of accommodating mid-sized vessels have been carved into the largest chambers, their entrances concealed by obsidian overhangs. The complex appears currently unoccupied, but power systems remain on standby.

The identity and purpose of Bunker Obsidis's builders remains unknown, and the discovery has triggered a discreet intelligence scramble among regional powers. The complex's construction quality suggests military or paramilitary backing, and its location -- on a world specifically chosen for its near-invisibility -- implies operations that someone wanted kept very quiet. Whether this is a smuggler's haven, a covert military installation, or something else entirely, Bunker Obsidis has secrets that powerful parties would prefer remain buried.
